correctness.rationale: A direct reconstruction confirms the all-graph theorem over finite connected simple unit-edge graphs and real scalars. The finite free-space unit ball is the convex hull of directed edge molecules by shortest-path telescoping; its dual unit ball is the graph-Lipschitz polytope. At an extreme dual height, the tight-edge graph must connect all vertices, otherwise a nonroot tight component can be perturbed in both signs; integer heights follow. Each edge slope is -1,0,1. For a flat chosen edge uv, assigning auxiliary edge lengths w_ab=1-|h(a)-h(b)|/2 gives direct distance 1 from v to u, since the selected edge costs 1 and any alternative path has at least two edges of cost >=1/2. The rooted potential k(z)=d_w(v,z)-d_w(v,o) yields g_+=k+h/2 and g_-=k-h/2, both original-metric norm-one functionals norming m_uv and satisfying h=g_+-g_-. Extreme dual evaluations of Tm_uv are <=v(T) at slope +/-1 and <=2v(T) at slope 0, proving ||T||<=2v(T). For K3 the explicit matrix [[-1/2,0],[1,1/2]] in delta basis has norm 1 and numerical radius 1/2, proving sharpness. A newly written exact rational/integer checker (not the uploaded verifier) independently covered 48 connected graph instances (all labeled connected n=2,3,4 plus 5 selected n=5), 556 flat-edge decompositions, the exact gauge equivalence to the other published proof, and K3 norm/radius. These finite checks corroborate but cannot replace the all-finite-n analytic argument.
